svg.title: iOS · Launch · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/LaunchAnimationView.swift + App/LLRigMark.swift: the cold-launch holding state, drawn here at its settled frame. The rig assembles itself over ~2.05s and the wordmark rises at 1.78s; SVGs don't promise animation, so the beat sheet is recorded here instead — 0.10s pipe rim draws from 12 o'clock · 0.44/0.53s back legs punch down and overshoot · 0.51s pipe colour floods under the line · 0.58s board outline draws · 0.71/0.80s front legs drop · 0.85s lens ring draws · 0.95s board fill lands · 1.12s rim cools amber to #6E7F99 · 1.22s iris opens · 1.26–1.51s interval pads pop clockwise 85ms apart · 1.46s board rim cools to #245A85 · 1.67s glint · 1.78s wordmark rises 9pt. Cold launch ONLY (ContentView's showLaunch is @State, and is not rebuilt on a warm foreground); Reduce Motion skips the assembly and shows this frame for 0.6s. DARK IN BOTH APPEARANCES by design: the mark's home is the app icon's navy, and Create opens straight into the camera, so a light launch would seam into a black viewfinder a moment later. The status bar is hidden while the mark is up. The mark keeps its OWN palette — amber #F0A32C is the app icon's, NOT LL.accent (#C36A00) or LL.amber (#FFB340) — and no LL token appears on this screen. The static launch screen behind this is the same navy (App/Info.plist UILaunchScreen → UIColorName → LaunchBackground); without it an empty UILaunchScreen paints systemBackground, i.e. white, and holds it for seconds on a first install while dyld loads MLX. Hand-off: the camera cover slides up over a still-opaque field and the field is dropped 0.45s later, so the light Create screen is never exposed. Flow screen — no tab bar.
svg.text: mirrors App/LaunchAnimationView.swift — settled frame of the ~2.05s build
